command: TORCHFDTD_G3_FULL=1 TORCHFDTD_G3_RECORD=docs/validation/g3 D:/TorchFDTD/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_physics_g3_b.py -k g3_04 --junitxml=D:/TorchFDTD/.local/tmp/junit/G3-04.xml

physics_configuration.method: Closed TFSF box, six (3D) or four (2D) scattered-field monitor planes outside the box, matched empty-box reference run subtracted, incident intensity from a monitor inside the box of the empty run; cross section = outward scattered power / incident intensity. Yee material sampling, staircase interface, native CPML with the physical thickness below on every face.

cylinder.dimension: 2d, propagation along +x, cylinder axis along the invariant z
cylinder.pulse: Gaussian, centre 1.55 um, power FWHM 8 fs, offset 30 fs

sphere.pulse: Gaussian, centre 1.55 um, power FWHM 8 fs, offset 30 fs
sphere.grid_at_judged_mesh: 48^3 (the CUDA cap of the recorded run); 0.025 um is 96^3 and runs on the CPU in FP64 only

resonance.dimension: 2d, TE (Ey), same domain, box, monitors and PML as the cylinder
resonance.resonance: TE peak of the Mie scattering width near 1.136 um, full width at half maximum about 0.065 um (Q about 17); the sharper TM peak near 1.10 um is outside this band's pulse and not judged
resonance.peak_definition: parabolic refinement through the three samples around the maximum of the sampled curve; FWHM by linear interpolation of the sampled curve at half of the refined peak height; the same procedure is applied to the Mie curve sampled at the same 61 wavelengths

physics_configuration.layer_a: the same discrete problem on fused CUDA FP32 (RTX 3060) and the CPU FP64 reference path at every mesh at or below 48^3 cells; the cross-section observable is compared

reference_method: Infinite-cylinder Mie series (TM and TE coefficients from continuity of the axial field and of its normal derivative divided by mu or epsilon; C = (4/k) sum over all integer orders of |c_n|^2) and Bohren-Huffman sphere series, both written in tests/test_physics_g3_b.py with SciPy Bessel functions and checked against the optical theorem, the small-size limits and the repository's independent real-index sphere series in examples/tfsf_sphere.py. No solver routine enters the reference.

observables.name: scattering_width_um
observables.definition: 2D outward scattered power per unit length through the four monitor lines divided by the incident intensity, nine wavelengths

observables.name: scattering_cross_section_um2
observables.definition: 3D outward scattered power through the six monitor planes divided by the incident intensity, nine wavelengths

observables.name: max_relative_error
observables.definition: max over the nine wavelengths of |measured/Mie - 1|

observables.name: resonance_peak_um
observables.definition: refined peak wavelength of the TE scattering width of the 0.25 um, n = 3.5 cylinder

observables.name: resonance_fwhm_um
observables.definition: full width at half maximum of that peak

observables.name: layer_a_relative_difference
observables.definition: CUDA FP32 cross section divided by the CPU FP64 cross section minus one, per wavelength

acceptance_limits.judged_at: cylinder: h = 0.0125 um for TM and TE; sphere: h = 0.05 um; the coarser meshes of each sequence are recorded and not judged
acceptance_limits.monotonicity: not required; staircased curved surfaces are allowed a non-monotone error sequence and the record keeps every mesh

resonance.justification: the staircase perturbs the effective radius by a fraction of the cell and the internal wavelength is resolved by about 26 cells at the judged mesh; both shift the resonance by a few tenths of a percent, so 1 percent on the position is a first engineering target; the width of a Q = 17 resonance is the difference of two flank positions and is given a proportionally looser 15 percent

layer_a_cuda_fp32_vs_cpu_fp64.source: completion_gates.json proposed_thresholds discrete_dimensionless_fp32 applied to the cross-section observable

acceptance_limits.source_of_limits: completion_gates.json proposed_thresholds mie_integrated_cross_section_relative_error; the resonance and layer-A budgets are fixture-specific and stated above

applicable_scope: Layer B physics of the 2D cylinder (TM, TE, resonance) and the 3D sphere against the Mie series on the CPU FP64 reference path, and layer A CUDA FP32 (fused kernel, RTX 3060) against CPU FP64 at every grid at or below 48^3 cells; staircase interface, closed TFSF box, native CPML.
note: Run in Git Bash with TMP and TEMP set to D:/TorchFDTD/.local/tmp; the four task runs executed concurrently on the shared workstation while other agents used the GPU, so wall times in the record are not performance measurements. The hostname attribute was removed from the JUnit report before recording.
